messages:
oncall-bot: paging #eng-sre — p99 latency for /v1/generate spiked to ~7s, error rate (502/504) climbing to 15% over the last 5m. auto-alert threshold breached.
ops-bot: incident created INC-2028-234, priority: P1. Notifying on-call.
alex: seeing same in dashboards — p95 ~3s, p99 ~7s, throughput steady. Gateway 502s correlated with canary deploy canary/v3.8.1-rc2 at 1854321500.
maya: confirmed. Canary started ~10m before alert. Logs show increased backend timeouts hitting inference pool.
sam: quick sanity check — any throttling from LB or token bucket changes?
alex: LB steady. No config change besides canary. Queue length on inference workers up ~3x.
jen (oncall): I'm taking this. Rolling canary back now to previous stable v3.8.0. Initiating rollback in k8s:
```
kubectl -n inference set image deployment/api-proxy proxy=image:redwood/api-proxy:v3.8.0
kubectl rollout status deploy/api-proxy -w
```
jen (oncall): also opening ticket for CS: possible customer impact on streaming generation. @support-bot please notify support triage.
support-bot: support alert sent: ETA to customers updated. Suggested message: "We're investigating intermittent generation timeouts affecting some requests. Working on a fix and will update in 30m."
ops-bot: rollback job started by jen at 1854321994. Canary traffic will be drained.
chris: putting fallback routing in place to route to model-small when latency > 2s for user-facing routes. Patch: feature-flag route-fallback=true.
maya: quick note — KV cache hit rate dropped after the new model changed cache key shape, meaning cache misses spiked, causing overload. If rollback succeeds, cache behavior should revert.
sam: can we also raise replica count temporarily? If cache miss is high we'll need capacity.
jen (oncall): scaling inference-deployment +2 replicas now: `kubectl scale deploy/inference --replicas=8`
alex: metrics show error rate starting to fall — 502s down to ~6% after rollback started. p99 trending down.
ops-bot: rollback completed at 1854322031. Deploys stable at v3.8.0.
jen (oncall): verifying end-to-end: running smoke test against /v1/generate (10 reqs, 1k tokens)
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":64}' | jq .
```
jen (oncall): smoke tests passed 10/10 with median latency 450ms.
alex: Grafana shows p95 back to ~250ms, p99 ~600ms. Error rate ~0.7% now.
jen (oncall): marking incident as mitigated. Creating postmortem stub and assigning owners: infra/maya (root cause), eng-runtime/alex (rollback/metrics), platform/chris (fallback routing).
ops-bot: attaching timeline and alerts to INC-2028-234.
jen (oncall): handing off to next on-call for watch: @ria — I did the rollback and scaling, please watch for regressions for the next hour and own comms to CS if anything changes.
ria: ack — I'll monitor for 60m, I've got dashboard links and alert playbook open.
chris: customer impact: flagged 3 support tickets tied to higher latency; support-bot please attach incident link to those tickets and set priority to High.
support-bot: attached INC-2028-234 to tickets #7891, #7892, #7893 and updated customers.
maya: preliminary RCA note: canary introduced model change which altered cache key behavior => cache miss storm => backend queueing => timeouts. Need change in model onboarding tests to validate cache key stability.
jen (oncall): agreed. Action items: (1) revert model onboarding checklist to include cache-key smoke tests (owner: maya), (2) add pre-deploy traffic shaping for canaries (owner: chris), (3) add alert for cache hit-rate delta > 10% (owner: alex). Setting 24h follow-up.
alex: adding grafana alert for cache-hit-rate-delta and linking to runbook.
jen (oncall): closing thread here, incident transitioned to postmortem. If any spike within the watch window @ria will re-open. Thanks all :thumbsup:
ria: thx, keeping an eye.
